content: Is there any trick to mark a lemma as something positivity should always apply? I’m worried the answer is no because of https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/fa89eff14f58e554df4001c58e3d3b8adb64ebb5/Mathlib/Topology/MetricSpace/Pseudo/Defs.lean#L253-L268 which is incredibly tedious compared to the expected method that would simply add an attribute to dist_nonneg. I have a project with a lot of positive stuff, and that boilerplate is pretty painful.

Related question: is there anyway to debug positivity extensions? I was able to find two trace classes related to positivity, but none of them seem to show which extensions are tried and the error messages they throw.

Pan Lin (supervised by Floris) is working on the former: Floris just told me "it's very close to a mathlib PR being opened". The code is working, documented and tested (but will need review, of course).
For the latter, see @Eric Wieser's #43631
@Pan Lin opened #44923 that adds a @[positivity_lemma] attribute. He will split the work into smaller PRs, the first one is #45072.
